narrative:
The model predicted that you have a 52.7% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability tips just above 50%, the admissions system automatically rejected your law school application.

The decision was driven primarily by three aspects of your academic record. Your class ranking in the third year of law school was the strongest factor pushing the prediction toward failure. Placing in the second decile is noticeably lower than the average of roughly sixth-decile performance among students who were accepted, and this weaker standing strongly signaled higher risk of struggling on the bar. Your first-year ranking in the third decile reinforced that concern, though it carried less weight than the third-year result.

Your undergraduate GPA of 3.30 worked in the opposite direction. It sits slightly above the 3.23 average of accepted students and therefore pulled the prediction modestly toward passing. Unfortunately, this positive signal was not large enough to overcome the impact of your law-school class rankings.

Given the model’s outcome, you should focus on strengthening the areas that mattered most. Retaking key courses to improve your class standing, seeking targeted bar-prep support, or gaining additional practical legal experience could raise your future predicted success rate. Reapply once you have clear evidence of improvement in academic performance.
